text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- A majority on parliament's finance committee has decided to investigate once more the crisis in the banking sector in the late 1980s. Nearly 190,000 private investors lost money when Norwegian banks nearly collapsed and had to be resuced by the government.
- The United States has criticised Norway for hindering free trade. According to a recent report America's trade deficit to Norway increased by $514 million to $2.4 billion in 1996.

- The share price of Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA rose to a record high 383.50 crowns per A-share on Friday after the company posted better than expected first-quarter results.
- Fewer people want to become teachers. This year there were 1,071 fewer applicants than in 1996 for teaching courses. Low salary is propably the main reason for declining interest.
- Industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA has signed a letter of intent to build a fertilizer plant in Argentina worth four billion crowns.

- Major shareholders in Orkla ASA could decide to ask head of the company, Jens Heyerdahl, to resign if he decides to vote against the proposed merger between Norway's largest insurer, Storebrand, and commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Orkla holds a 10 percent stake in Storebrand.
